<thought>To determine the number of methyl (CH₃) groups in the unknown sample, the most direct approach is to examine its 13C NMR spectrum. Methyl carbons appear in the upfield region (≈10–30 ppm). By counting the distinct methyl carbon signals, we can infer the number of methyl groups present (equivalent methyls give a single signal, but the question asks for the total number of CH₃ groups, not distinct signals). Therefore, I will first obtain the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
